methodological_rigor.justification: Single-center retrospective cohort of 575 patients with no power calculation, no external validation cohort for the ML models, and no propensity-score matching for the treatment comparisons (afatinib vs gefitinib/erlotinib; bevacizumab vs none). Subgroup analyses are small (n=35 vs 36 for bevacizumab line comparisons; n=3-13 for rare EGFR subtypes) and the authors acknowledge selection bias in later-line comparisons. Missing-data handling uses complete-case exclusion without imputation, and 20.6% of patients have unknown EGFR status. On the positive side, the authors apply the TSHRC method for non-proportional hazards and report HRs with 95% CIs; however multiplicity across 26 variables and multiple subgroup tests is not corrected, and no sensitivity analyses are reported. ML modeling uses a reasonable panel of 5 methods but only a single 70/30 split (no cross-validation or external hold-out) and no calibration assessment.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual single-center retrospective cohort = Oxford LoE 2b. The question (prognostic factors and OS in advanced lung adenocarcinoma) is clinically meaningful and OS is patient-relevant, but nearly all findings reinforce established knowledge (EGFR-mutation benefit, afatinib performance, smoking as adverse factor). The ML models reach only modest performance (best C-index ~0.70) and are not externally validated, so they cannot yet translate into a clinically deployable risk-stratification tool. The Taiwan reimbursement context excluding first-line osimertinib limits contemporary applicability of the first-line TKI comparisons.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE applies to this observational cohort. No STROBE checklist or patient-flow diagram is provided; inclusion/exclusion criteria are minimal ('No other specific inclusion or exclusion criteria were applied'), and no account is given of how patients were sampled from the 1,190 adenocarcinoma cases to arrive at 575. Follow-up duration, censoring handling, loss to follow-up, and the number of events are not clearly reported. TRIPOD-style reporting for the prediction models is also absent (no calibration, no decision-curve analysis, no reporting of model specifications beyond the library used). No data-availability statement, no code repository, and no supplementary protocol are provided.

novelty_literature.justification: The empirical findings are confirmatory of well-established literature: EGFR mutations prolong OS, afatinib outperforms first-generation TKIs, smoking is an adverse prognostic factor, and exon 20 insertions carry poor prognosis. Applying five off-the-shelf survival ML models (RSF, Cox-elastic-net, SVM, GBS, decision rule) to a single-center cohort is methodologically unremarkable; no novel feature engineering, model architecture, or clinical decision framework is introduced. The population (Taiwanese advanced lung adenocarcinoma 2010-2019) is adequately covered by prior work (e.g., references 11, 12, 29). The 'notable innovations' claimed in the introduction (combining stats with ML, 26 features, time-dependent C-index) are standard practice rather than genuine novelty.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is generally readable and logically organized into standard sections, with an abstract that accurately summarizes the main findings. However, there are typographical issues (e.g., 'erotinib' for erlotinib in the abstract), awkward phrasing ('cancer had a higher malignancy'), and an off-topic sentence noting bevacizumab's use in ovarian cancer within the lung-cancer discussion. The discussion partly rehashes results and includes some unsupported speculation ('we hypothesize that permetrexed chemotherapy may explain the prolongation of OS'). Figure captions appear adequate for standalone interpretation but descriptions in the text do not always match the stated numerics (e.g., L861Q median OS stated as 50.9 months in results but 50.8 months in discussion).

key_strengths: Reasonable cohort size (n=575) with a decade of real-world Taiwanese advanced lung adenocarcinoma data and OS as a hard endpoint
Appropriate use of the TSHRC method to address non-proportional hazards, with HRs and 95% CIs reported
Comparative panel of five survival ML models evaluated with time-dependent C-index and AUC
Clinically coherent prognostic findings consistent with established literature (EGFR status, smoking, afatinib)
key_concerns: Single-center retrospective design with no external validation of ML models and no power/sample-size justification
Important selection bias in treatment comparisons (afatinib vs older TKIs; bevacizumab line effects) with no propensity matching or sensitivity analyses
20.6% unknown EGFR status handled by complete-case exclusion; no imputation; no multiplicity correction across 26 variables and many subgroup tests
Reporting gaps vs STROBE/TRIPOD: no flow diagram, no event counts/censoring details, no calibration or decision-curve analysis, no data/code availability
Novelty is limited: findings are largely confirmatory and ML modeling uses off-the-shelf survival algorithms with modest C-index (~0.70) and single 70/30 split
Minor presentation issues including typos (e.g., 'erotinib'), inconsistent numerics (L861Q OS 50.9 vs 50.8 months), and off-topic ovarian-cancer tangent in the discussion
chief_reviewer.rationale: The paper is a competently executed but highly incremental single-center retrospective cohort with limited methodological novelty, no external validation, and significant reporting gaps; it is best suited to a Tier 4 outlet after major revisions addressing bias, multiplicity, and reporting-standard adherence.
